rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is establishing a performance floor. Config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-2000) is the simplest, most standard baseline in the design space. It tests how much signal RNA alone provides with a straightforward linear dimensionality reduction, giving a reference point against which to measure the incremental value of (a) image modality, (b) learned RNA encoders (scvi, scGPT), (c) multiprofile aggregation, and (d) multimodal fusion. Establishing this floor first ensures that in the remaining 9 experiments I can make informed exploitation/exploration trade-offs rather than assuming complexity will help. It is also the lowest-cost configuration to run, allowing a quick readout to guide the next step.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: RNA-only, PCA, single-profile at ~48.5% acc), the highest-uncertainty question is whether the image modality carries useful signal for this task. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the simplest image-only baseline and directly answers this. If image-only accuracy is competitive or strong, the large multimodal subspace (configs 16-51) becomes a promising exploitation target for the remaining 7 experiments. If it is weak, we can deprioritize multimodal configs and focus on RNA encoder improvements (scvi, scgpt) or multiprofile aggregation. This is a clean single-variable shift (modality) from the baseline, keeping profile setting and complexity level comparable, so the result isolates the value of visual information. Under a 10-experiment budget, resolving the modality question early is the most information-dense use of experiment 2.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieved 0.485 accuracy while image (ResNet50) was very weak at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether a learned representation (scVI) can outperform the linear PCA baseline on the same single-profile setup. This experiment (config_004: scvi_n200, single profile) directly isolates the encoder effect by changing only the RNA encoder from PCA to scVI while keeping profile setting and architecture identical to config_001. If scVI improves over PCA, it justifies investing remaining budget in stronger encoders (scGPT) and multimodal fusion with better representations. If it does not, PCA is sufficient and we should pivot to testing multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. This is the highest-information single change given 7 experiments remain.

Evidence: scvi_n200 singleprofile (config_004, acc=0.520) is the best result so far, clearly outperforming pca_n2000 singleprofile (0.485) and image-only resnet50 (0.208). The dominant signal is RNA, and the scvi encoder is the strongest RNA representation tested. Uncertainty: We have no evidence yet on whether multiprofile aggregation adds value over singleprofile. This experiment tests exactly that: it extends the best configuration (scvi_n200) to multiprofile with a simple avgpool aggregation, isolating the profile-setting effect while keeping the encoder fixed. If multiprofile+avgpool improves over 0.520, it justifies further investment in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, multimodal fusion). If it does not, we can redirect remaining budget toward scgpt or multimodal exploration. This is the highest-information single-variable step under the remaining 6-experiment budget.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over the singleprofile baseline (0.520). The key open question is whether the aggregation method can be improved: transformer aggregation could capture richer inter-profile relationships compared to simple avgpool. config_006 is a clean single-variable comparison (avgpool → transformer) holding all else constant (scvi_n200, multiprofile, rna_only), directly isolating the aggregation effect on the best-performing setup. This is the highest-value next step because: (1) it exploits the strongest evidence by testing a logical extension, (2) the answer will determine whether transformer aggregation is worth pursuing in the remaining multimodal configurations, and (3) with 5 experiments left, confirming or ruling out the aggregation upgrade early lets the remaining budget focus on encoder choice or multimodal fusion with confidence.

Evidence: Multiprofile with scvi_n200 is the clear winner so far (0.650-0.653), far exceeding singleprofile RNA (0.485-0.520) and image-only (0.208). Aggregation (avgpool vs transformer) shows negligible difference (~0.3%). The untested variable with the most potential upside is the RNA encoder: scgpt has never been tested, and as a pretrained generative model it may capture richer biological structure than scvi_n200. Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile setting, or is scvi_n200 already near-optimal for RNA representation? This is a clean single-variable comparison against the current best (config_006), isolating the encoder effect while holding profile and aggregation fixed. Why now: With 4 experiments remaining, establishing the best RNA encoder before committing to multimodal fusion experiments ensures subsequent multimodal trials use the strongest backbone. If scgpt multiprofile matches or beats 0.653, it opens a new exploitation path; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 and can pivot remaining budget to multimodal fusion with confidence.

Evidence: RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 + transformer (config_006, acc=0.653) is the current best, and multiprofile + scvi_n200 is clearly the strongest RNA setup. Image-only with resnet50 was very weak (0.208), but we have not yet tested the stronger imagenet_vit_l encoder. The key uncertainty is whether a powerful image encoder can provide complementary signal to the already-strong RNA representation, or whether it will only add noise. This experiment (config_038) takes the best RNA configuration (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) and adds imagenet_vit_l with concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion can exceed 0.653. It is the highest-value test because: (1) it isolates the effect of adding a strong image modality to the proven-best RNA pipeline, (2) concat is the simpler fusion choice reducing confounds, and (3) with only 3 experiments remaining, we need to determine early whether the multimodal direction is viable or whether we should focus remaining budget on RNA-only refinements.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.7207 accuracy. The only untested variation of this exact configuration is the fusion method: weighted vs. concat. Config_039 isolates this single design choice, making it a clean A/B comparison. Evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 over scgpt (0.65 vs 0.51 in RNA-only multiprofile), multiprofile over single profile, and imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (implied by the large multimodal gain). Transformer aggregation was marginally better than avgpool in RNA-only (0.653 vs 0.650), so keeping transformer is reasonable. Testing weighted fusion is the highest-value next step because it directly probes whether the current best can be improved with a minimal, well-isolated change, and with only 2 experiments remaining after this one, exploiting the strongest configuration is the right strategy.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 acc. The two top configs (038 concat vs 039 weighted) differ by only 0.4%, and in the RNA-only setting transformer vs avgpool differed by only 0.3% (0.653 vs 0.650). Config_037 tests avgpool aggregation while keeping all other settings identical to the best config (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of aggregation in the multimodal context, clarifying whether transformer aggregation provides a meaningful advantage over simpler avgpool when combined with the strongest image encoder. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, confirming or ruling out the aggregation choice within the proven best family is the highest-value use of the next slot—it either validates the current best or reveals a comparable alternative without risking a large performance drop from changing the encoder or modality.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. The completed experiments have tested 3 of the 4 cells in the aggregation×fusion grid for this top multimodal family: transformer+concat (0.7207), transformer+weighted (0.7250), and avgpool+weighted (0.7062). Config_036 (avgpool+concat) is the only remaining cell. Testing it completes the 2×2 interaction grid, confirming whether the transformer+weighted advantage is due to a genuine synergy or simply the sum of two independent effects. Since this is the final experiment and all individually superior design choices (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) have already been combined in config_039, no untested configuration is likely to exceed 0.7250. Config_036 is the most informative remaining test within the top-performing model family, providing a clean isolation of the aggregation–fusion interaction without introducing a new, weaker component.
